A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoSNet work. All 16 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v2, including figures, tables, mathematical notation, and appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet evaluations, training-time measurements, MS-COCO detection results, architectural ablations, and activation-map analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds batch-size comparisons, RetinaNet detection results, and PSPNet semantic-segmentation results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.8 retain the same parallel columns, input replication, batched execution, fusion schemes, and shallow/deep projections. Pairwise Frequent Fusion already appears in v1, and Appendix A's model configurations are unchanged. The new downstream evaluations describe no architectural adaptation.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates ImageNet classification and MS-COCO object detection. v2 adds semantic segmentation through PSPNet (Appendix D, Table A5), substantially extending task coverage. The segmentation dataset is not identified, so a specific additional dataset cannot be established.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds InceptionNeXt-S and UniRepLKNet-S while retaining all existing comparators. The added downstream comparisons use EfficientViT-M4 in RetinaNet and RepVGG-B1g2/ResNet-50 in PSPNet (Tables A4–A5). These extend the comparison set without replacing its established coverage.

E3.justification: v2 adds comparisons at training batch sizes 256 versus 2048/4096, a RetinaNet 'x1' evaluation, and PSPNet evaluation using mIoU/FPS. Existing ImageNet splits, batch-1 latency measurements, and ablation budgets are unchanged. The newly disclosed batch-256 training basis for retained Table 1 results does not establish a between-version protocol change.

E4.justification: Appendix C and Table A3 add an analysis of baseline accuracy at different training batch sizes, contextualizing comparisons with CoSNet trained at batch 256. The architectural ablations in Appendix B/Table A2 and activation-map analysis in Figure 6 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added tables continue the existing practice of reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Previously reported numerical values are retained, but v2 substantially expands the outcomes: Table 1 adds 83.5%/83.9% top-1 accuracy for InceptionNeXt-S/UniRepLKNet-S, and Table A3 adds larger-batch baseline results. Table A4 reports RetinaNet AP of 34.3 for CoSNet-A0 versus 32.7 for EfficientViT-M4. Table A5 reports PSPNet mIoU of 79.05 for CoSNet-B1 versus 78.88/77.17 for RepVGG-B1g2/ResNet-50. These are additional comparisons, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 3's input-replication tensor definition, kernel constraints, and architectural parameter relationships are unchanged. No mathematical derivation, formal assumption, theorem, or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same claims about concise CoSNet architectures and competitive accuracy, depth, parameter, computation, and runtime tradeoffs. The additional experiments support these existing contributions without redefining the central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly interprets CoSNet's competitiveness at batch 256 against larger-batch baselines as evidence of usefulness under training-memory constraints. Existing mechanism explanations remain unchanged. The paragraph renamed from 'Limitations' to 'Future work' retains its substantive content.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents batch-256 training for CoSNet and the baseline retraining underlying Table 1. It removes v1's post-review code-release and code-snippet announcement; neither PDF actually contains the promised listing. The repository link and PyTorch/eight-NVIDIA-A40 hardware disclosure remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for InceptionNeXt, UniRepLKNet, RetinaNet, PSPNet, and PyTorch. The positioning around simple, concise ConvNets remains substantially unchanged. Correcting VanillaNet's citation year does not introduce a different prior work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose and citation-style edits, updates author/publication information, adds acknowledgements, and renames 'Limitations' to 'Future work.' New appendix sections shift the training-setting and visualization sections, while the main narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables A3–A5 and two comparator rows to Table 1, causing localized reflow. Figure A1 moves from page 16 to page 17. Existing figures, including the architecture diagrams, performance plots, and activation maps, retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency by explaining the training-batch basis of existing comparisons and reporting larger-batch baseline results. Recent comparators and additional downstream evaluations broaden validation. However, the new downstream protocols remain sparsely documented, especially the unnamed segmentation dataset, limiting the strength of the added evidence. The net improvement is useful but limited.
